answer_1.quote: Over the past few years, Machine Translation (MT) evaluation metrics have transitioned from heuristic-based to neural-based, enabling a more nuanced evaluation of translation quality and a greater agreement with human judgments.

answer_2.quote: we evaluate MT metrics performance in two settings: i) when metrics are used as binary classifiers, tasked to separate between GOOD and BAD translations (acting as a proxy for the data filtering application), and ii) when metrics are used to identify the best translation in a group of translations of the same source (acting as a proxy for translation re-ranking).

answer_3.quote: GEMBA-MQM leverages GPT-4 to produce detailed quality assessments.

answer_4.quote: Both datasets consist of source texts translated by multiple MT systems, with translation quality assessed by professional human annotators.
answer_4.guideline: Within the MQM annotation framework, professional annotators identify span-level translation errors and assign each error a category and severity.
